tools.name: lint_x402_endpoint
tools.description: Unpaid lint of an x402 endpoint: fetches the 402 (GET and POST), then checks the challenge (version, accepts[] fields, CAIP-2 network, payTo/asset/amount sanity, EIP-712 name/version, timeouts, resource), transport (redirects, cache headers, CORS) and discovery files. Returns findings with ids, seve

tools.name: check_directory_readiness
tools.description: Lint an x402 endpoint's unpaid 402 and report, per directory, whether it meets what x402dash (unpaid GET must return 402), x402scan (OpenAPI x-payment-info or /.well-known/x402, input schema), the402 (validator 'payable') and the CDP/PayAI Bazaar (bazaar extension, description <= 500 chars, non-tunn

tools.name: lint_payment_required
tools.description: Lint a PaymentRequired object you already have (decoded JSON, a JSON string, or the raw base64 PAYMENT-REQUIRED header). Same field/value checks as lint_x402_endpoint, no network access. Free.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: lint_x402_endpoint · Private data: lint_x402_endpoint · Public sink: lint_x402_endpoint.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: lint_x402_endpoint · Private data: lint_x402_endpoint · Public sink: lint_x402_endpoint

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
